ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: The figure is a schematic map of a weather situation, and the labeled L1, L2, M, and N can be seen. N is located in the lower-left part of the figure, close to the linear position near L1; the linear position shown by L1—L2 extends from near place N toward the northeast. There are diagonally shaded areas on the right side and southeast side of the figure, but their meaning needs to be judged in combination with the cold wave orange alert information in the question stem.
Then reason: The cold wave orange alert in the question stem indicates that strong cold air is moving eastward and southward, and the relevant areas will have relatively strong northerly winds in the next two days; combined with place N in the figure being close to the weather system position near L1—L2, it can be judged that place N will be affected by the cold wave cold-air process in the next two days. When a cold wave passes through, it is often accompanied by strong winds, increased cloud amount, or precipitation, and daytime warming by solar radiation is suppressed; at night, due to cloud insulation and enhanced atmospheric mixing, the decrease in minimum temperature is relatively limited, and the gap between the maximum temperature and minimum temperature narrows. Therefore, the daily temperature range of place N in the figure will become smaller in the next two days.
